info.desc: Plastic Beach is the third studio album by English virtual band Gorillaz, released March 3, 2010 on Parlophone and Virgin Records. Conceived from an unfinished Gorillaz project called "Carousel", the album was recorded during June 2008 to November 2009 and produced primarily by group co-creator Damon Albarn. It features guest appearances by several artists, including Snoop Dogg, Gruff Rhys, Bobby Womack, Mos Def, Lou Reed, Mick Jones, and the Hypnotic Brass Ensemble. Primarily a pop album, "Plastic Beach" contains lyrics concerning consumerism and ecology-related themes. The album has produced three singles, "Stylo", "Superfast Jellyfish", and "On Melancholy Hill". Creators of .

podcast.body: The third album, initially titled "Carousel," was released on March 3, 2010. Its final title and concept were inspired by Damon Albarn's depression over plastic trash on a beach, tying into the environmental issue of the Great Pacific Garbage Patch. The album's music was designed to be much more pop-oriented than its predecessors and featured an extensive list of collaborators. "As for the music, it's much more pop than the first two records. That was by design from the outset."

podcast.body: This album suffered a significant commercial failure and had a reduction in promotional spending, despite being planned as an ambitious three-album project over several years which ultimately fell apart. Musically, it represented a shift towards a more sophisticated, less commercial, and less accessible sound, making it particularly favored by critics and more "cultivated" fans. "Había en sufrido un importante fracaso comercial en sus dos trabajos anteriores, tanto en Plastic Beach como en Default, había bastantes disputas internas entre los dos miembros más importantes."
